answer:
Let the two circle coordinates be \(U,V\in[0,1)\) i.i.d. uniform. The shorter arc length is

\[
D=\min\{|U-V|,\,1-|U-V|\}.
\]

For \(0\le d\le \tfrac12\),

\[
\Pr(D\le d)=\Pr(|U-V|\le d \text{ or } |U-V|\ge 1-d).
\]

In the unit square \([0,1]^2\), the area with \(|U-V|\le d\) is \(2d-d^2\), and the area with \(|U-V|\ge 1-d\) is \(d^2\). Thus

\[
F_D(d)=(2d-d^2)+d^2=2d,
\]

so \(D\) is uniform on \([0,\tfrac12]\), with density

\[
f_D(d)=2,\qquad 0\le d\le \tfrac12.
\]

Therefore

\[
\Pr(D>0.2)=1-F_D(0.2)=1-2(0.2)=0.6=\frac35.
\]

Also,

\[
\mathbb E[D]=\int_0^{1/2} d\cdot 2\,dd
= \left[d^2\right]_0^{1/2}
=\frac14.
\]

Check by fixing the first point: by rotational symmetry fix it at \(0\). The second point has clockwise coordinate \(X\sim \mathrm{Unif}(0,1)\), and

\[
D=\min(X,1-X).
\]

Then

\[
\Pr(D\le d)=\Pr(X\le d)+\Pr(X\ge 1-d)=d+d=2d,
\]

and

\[
\mathbb E[D]=\int_0^1 \min(x,1-x)\,dx
=2\int_0^{1/2}x\,dx=\frac14,
\]

which agrees.

\[
\boxed{\Pr(D>0.2)=\frac35=0.6,\qquad \mathbb E[D]=\frac14=0.25.}
\]

If you meant the conditional expectation given \(D>0.2\), then

\[
\mathbb E[D\mid D>0.2]
=\frac{\int_{0.2}^{0.5} d(2)\,dd}{0.6}
=\frac{0.21}{0.6}=0.35.
\]

But the ordinary expected value of \(D\) is \(\boxed{0.25}\).
